reviews.rationale: All functions validate or execute one managed deliberation lifecycle and share the same provider plan, writing contract, checkpoint, and interruption semantics. Participant route validation, verified role composition, and organization-event mutation are isolated in the deliberation participant binding module; this module only orders binding, round execution, terminal release, and the existing lifecycle boundaries.

The module sequences one admitted run through context, execution, outcome checks, writing publication, finalization, and cleanup. Public command contracts, provider construction, grounded capability selection and package ceilings, and outcome verification are separate modules. Existing research, role, skill, workspace and project-verification owners retain their boundaries; the remaining lifecycle shares one ordered failure and storage-cleanup contract.

TLS material loading, dependency and server composition, reload, resource lifecycle orchestration, and health wiring are phases of one Hub deployment boundary; HTTP connection-drain mechanics and domain policy remain in linked modules.

The class resolves one conversation event to a mode and dispatches its response through injected ports. Discussion eligibility, effect admission, intent conversion, and discussion response policy remain in dedicated modules; this boundary only selects the current event's available effects, caches its resolution, and routes the admitted result. ADR-0467 owner-turn capture is an injected port that only queues the turn.

The module composes one provider-neutral supervision runtime from storage, admission, reasoning, execution, and evidence ports. Request-origin evaluation, resource policy, provider effects, supersession, leases, snapshot projection, and wake scheduling with its observation gate remain in dedicated modules; this boundary only wires their ordered lifecycle and cleanup.

The class observes one bound goal for task, admission, owner-control, and cycle snapshots, and audits its history projection's tail for the wake schedule. It composes dedicated workforce, execution, authority, result, and handoff readers; effect execution, persistence, provider transport, domain policy, and runtime scheduling remain in separate modules. The two history projections share a canonical event chain but retain distinct task and authority scopes.

The class owns one external Claude protocol boundary and translates native session, tool, telemetry, stop, and result behavior into common adapter contracts; the accounting declaration remains in a linked descriptor module. The explicit login profile is snapshotted for this same provider-session lifecycle; environment construction and native process transport remain separate modules.

The class owns the Codex provider boundary, selects one injected native transport, and translates thread, turn, telemetry, stop, and result behavior into common adapter contracts; transport parsing and the accounting declaration remain linked modules. The explicit login profile is snapshotted for this same provider-session lifecycle; environment construction and native process transport remain separate modules.

The module executes one provider-neutral adapter conformance lifecycle from descriptor and session start through context, turn, telemetry, result identity, and stop; provider translation and focused binding rules remain in linked modules.

The repository class owns one SQLite persistence boundary for platform bindings, including validation, reads, writes, and transaction-safe state changes. Inbound depth and the optional ordered active-target projection use only identities resolved at that same mapping boundary; participation, discussion scheduling, and turn ownership policy remain outside the adapter.

The module owns one in-memory deliberation state machine; publication failure recording, handoff materialization, snapshot restoration, event recording, and ADR-0460 usage verification decisions remain in linked modules. Methods enforce shared history and event invariants, record each artifact's verification state, and refuse convergence on an unverified artifact. Policy-role names stay provider-neutral metadata.

The module owns the common event privacy boundary and its declarative allowlist and payload-schema registries. Provider admission, turn-bound selection, native-skill, and practice registrations add only declarative entries; native-skill and practice fields live in dedicated payload modules. Provider output interpretation, executable identity, transcript parsing, queue and marker persistence, query recording, reference detection, and scheduling stay in their owning adapters.

The declarative migration catalog and migration runner own one versioned SQLite schema boundary; length is driven by schema history rather than mixed runtime policy. The ADR-0466 owner lease, ADR-0467 instruction candidate, ADR-0469 host continuity, and ADR-0477 delegation-bound definition tables are additive migrations.

One SQLite adapter composes repositories under the shared database, transaction, and schema lifecycle. Notification retention and waiting live in a separate adapter; this facade emits only committed scope coordinates and closes notifications with the store. Owner-lease, instruction-candidate, ADR-0469 host-record, ADR-0477 definition, and ADR-0561 exact workstream revision methods only open a transaction around their own repositories.

One provider-neutral run lifecycle delegates source capture, process observation, capability policy, result collection and verification to existing ports. Source admission uses the project-storage gate for the complete run; failed reference-result preservation stays behind its own CAS/evidence boundary. The coordinator sequences both without owning SQLite or background retry policy.
The class owns one SQLite policy persistence boundary and its approval, verification, transaction, and query operations.

Declarative validation of one tracked layout contract: capacity, roles, routes with their prose descriptions, and legacy title terms read only for compatibility all report through the same JSON-pointer issue collector; loading, upgrade, and serialization live in the taxonomy module.

The module sequences one owner publication (repair, scope check, replay, push, pull request, merge, supersession, local catch-up) into one durable state and failure code. ADR-0473 scope rules, repair planning and commits, Git mechanics, forge transport, body rendering, tip building, supersession ledgers, and state persistence are sibling modules; the remaining functions share one progress and failure contract.

Publication rendering, historical-document grouping, desired output construction, recorded-output comparison, and plan creation are phases of one deterministic structural compilation contract; historical marker detection lives in its own module. Complete-scan refusal is shared with other currency consumers and applied at the common migration builder, including virtual scans. The configured reader remains partial-capable; private diagnostic persistence lives in scan-coverage.ts.

One reviewed rewrite lifecycle binds profiles, candidates, exact plans, and atomic apply. Observation, resource tracking, selection, caching, and tool ownership remain separate modules. The public compiler now delegates complete-coverage admission to the pure shared guard before provider calls; configured preparation and apply use the complete scanner. No independent scan or persistence policy is added.

Plan serialization, safe source inspection, merge planning, lineage updates, and apply are one atomic document-merge responsibility. Complete-scan admission is delegated to the shared configured scanner before this lifecycle operation; aggregate inventory fields retain their existing contract. No independent policy, provider, or persistence concern is added.

One exact-approved move binds destination safety, serialization, lineage, normalization record relocation and atomic apply. Shared modules retain record mechanics and layout policy. Complete scan admission delegates to the configured scanner before planning; no new independent responsibility is introduced.

Heading extraction, destination safety, plan serialization, lineage preservation, and apply are one atomic document-split responsibility. Complete-scan admission is delegated to the shared configured scanner before this lifecycle operation; aggregate inventory fields retain their existing contract. No independent policy, provider, or persistence concern is added.

One durable filesystem transaction owns staging, exact before/after bindings, publication, rollback and crash settlement. Apply snapshots operations, byte payloads and the document permit before acquiring its source gate; recovery captures the same root used for its gate. Terminal asset policy and validation remain in the runtime owner. Receipt interpretation stays with the caller; no provider or artifact policy enters the transaction.

Profile resolution, registry binding, structural refresh, plan creation, and exact-approved apply share one instruction-bridge lifecycle; target construction and classification are extracted. Complete-scan admission is delegated to the shared configured scanner before this lifecycle operation; aggregate inventory fields retain their existing contract. No independent policy, provider, or persistence concern is added.

Query behavior, safe publication access, and document drift findings were extracted; the rest validates manifests, layout, normalization, lineage, and semantic sidecars and composes drift and publication-root lint. Layout lint maps the shared evaluator's blocking findings to errors and capacity advisories to warnings (ADR-0583). The rewriter inspection gets lint's evidence sources only to share its scan (ADR-0582). Completeness admission stays in scan-completeness.ts.

One exact layout transaction with virtual scanning, exact item content binding, and apply-time revalidation. Accounting lives in repository-layout-accounting.ts and the ADR-0583 capacity hold in repository-layout-capacity.ts. Classification, route evidence, durable apply, providers, lifecycle authority, ADR-0561 reverted-move holds, and health keep separate owners.
Move, split, and merge lineage creation and validation operate on one lineage schema and safe registry-loading boundary.

Declarative repository knowledge contracts share scan, source, projection, query, lint, impact, and migration coordinates without runtime decisions or effects, including coverage and skipped summaries, the scan-incomplete reason, and the observed-only retention marker. ADR-0560 removed the refresh-review candidate contract. Evaluation, admission, storage, and rendering stay in their owning modules.

Current state, continuation import, start, update, and replicated import preserve one WorkstreamSnapshot aggregate, origin and predecessor invariants, CAS binding, plan identity, plan admission such as the ADR-0561 refusal of new approvals, and the durable apply protocol. Snapshot construction, bookkeeping, revisions, freshness, branch bindings, and context rendering live in sibling modules.

Identity calculation, registry validation, service-file inspection, onboarding planning, listing, and registration share one owner-only fleet registry contract; the exported service definition path is the same identity-to-path rule onboarding planning uses, so status readers cannot diverge from it.
The file is a declarative schema catalog for one adapter protocol; its length is data-shaped and contains no independent executable workflow.

The module contains only bounded JSON Schema declarations and inferred payload types for one organization-agent event catalog. Version-two deliberation participation fields extend the existing bound event additively; projection, privacy redaction, persistence, and execution remain in separate modules.

The module is the declarative schema-name catalog used by validation and generation. Provider admission, context-selected, native-skill, and practice payloads are catalog entries with the same mapping lifecycle; native-skill and practice schemas are defined in their own contract modules. Parsing, redaction, provider behavior, query recording, and persistence remain outside the catalog.

The module declares one terminal evidence lifecycle. Pointer fields, identities, reference kinds, and paired counts are additive. Equivalent nullable scalar schemas keep compiled validation within the measured hook bundle budget. Detection, persistence, privacy enforcement, and reporting remain separate.
Temporary project setup, process control, HTTPS calls, event observation, assertions, and cleanup compose one end-to-end acceptance scenario; command invocation is a separate thin entrypoint.

One coordinator owns exact predecessor validation, stable manager observations within the graceful stop bound, and transactional replacement for Hub, Node, host resident, replica coordinator, and host follower services; same-definition restarts are Node config transitions or ADR-0573 restarts. The renderer owns rendering and paths; transition selection, ADR-0489 recovery, and path-rewrite policy stay in adapters. Argument validation extraction remains the bounded roadmap follow-up.

The module composes the bounded suite, isolated workspaces, provider-neutral evidence selection, paired arm schedule, and cleanup; command invocation, versioned acceptance, report evaluation, provider preparation and transports, and selection policy remain separate.

The module owns one immutable comparison-contract lineage: protocols, schema, suite validation, and pure acceptance evaluation share the same version and gate lifecycle, while provider execution and evidence selection remain separate.

The module composes and validates one lineage of immutable provider-shadow contracts; policy, preparation I/O, execution, observation, and review remain in separate modules, while the length follows explicit historical contract variants.
